channel.title: The Dudley Blog
channel.description: Technology, App Store operations, app privacy, and software culture from Dudley Development.

item.title: What Does Offline-First Mean in an iPhone App?
item.description: Offline-first means an app can do its main job without a live internet connection. It is useful, but it is not the same thing as no data collection.

item.title: What Does Not Enough Ratings Mean on the App Store?
item.description: Not enough ratings means Apple is not displaying a public ratings overview for the app in that storefront yet. It does not prove an app has no users, no downloads, or low quality.

item.title: What Does Ready for Distribution Mean in App Store Connect?
item.description: Ready for Distribution means Apple has accepted the app version and it can be distributed, but it does not prove downloads, usage, revenue, or crash-free performance.

item.title: What Does No Account Required Mean in an iPhone App?
item.description: No account required usually means you can use the app without signing in. It does not automatically mean no data, no ads, no purchases, or no privacy label.

item.title: What Does Not Enough Data Mean in App Store Connect?
item.description: Not Enough Data usually means App Store Connect does not have enough eligible data to show a metric. It is not the same as zero installs, zero usage, or zero revenue.

item.title: What Are First-Time Downloads in App Store Connect?
item.description: First-Time Downloads show new App Store downloads, but they are not the same as active users, retention, revenue, or product-market fit.

item.title: What Is Age Assurance in Apps?
item.description: Age assurance is how an app or app store estimates, checks, or receives a user's age range so it can apply age-appropriate rules.

item.title: Does Google Photos Ask Photos Use Your Photos for AI Training?
item.description: Google says Gemini features in Google Photos do not use your personal Photos data for ads or to train generative AI models outside Google Photos.

item.title: What Are Content Credentials on AI Photos?
item.description: Content Credentials are provenance metadata that can show how a photo was created or edited.

item.title: Can You Remove the Gemini AI Watermark?
item.description: Gemini now lets some users turn off visible watermarks on AI-generated media.

item.title: What Is Nano Banana AI?
item.description: Nano Banana is Google's nickname for Gemini image generation and editing models.

item.title: Can iPhone Apps Tell When You Screen Record?
item.description: An iPhone app can often tell when its own screen is being recorded or mirrored, but that does not mean it can read the recording file or browse your old screen recordings.

item.title: Can iPhone Apps See Your Contacts?
item.description: An app needs Contacts access to browse your contacts. Apple's contact picker lets you share a contact without it, and newer iOS controls can limit access to selected people.

item.title: Does Visual Intelligence Send Photos to ChatGPT?
item.description: Visual Intelligence can send a photo, screenshot, or onscreen item to ChatGPT only when you choose a ChatGPT action.

item.title: What Does Limited Access Mean for Photos on iPhone?
item.description: Limited Access means an iPhone app can use only the photos and videos you select, not your whole photo library.

item.title: Does ChatGPT Use Your Photos To Train AI?
item.description: ChatGPT can use content you upload, including images, to improve OpenAI's models unless your plan or data controls say otherwise.

item.title: Does iPhone Share Photo Metadata When You Send a Picture?
item.description: Yes, iPhone photo sharing can include metadata such as date, time, location, device details, and captions.

item.title: Can iPhone Apps See Your Screenshots?
item.description: iPhone apps cannot automatically browse every screenshot, but an active app can know when you take a screenshot and photo permissions decide what screenshots you can share later.

item.title: Can People See Reels You Liked on Instagram?
item.description: Instagram likes are not always private. The Friends tab in Reels can surface public Reels your friends liked, commented on, reposted, or created, so check your activity controls before you treat a like as invisible.

item.title: Why Did My Photo Get a Made With AI Label?
item.description: A Made with AI label usually means a platform, tool, disclosure setting, or content credential signaled that media was meaningfully AI-generated or altered.

item.title: Can AI Photo Apps Use Your Photos To Train AI?
item.description: Some AI services can use saved media to improve models, but every photo app is different.

item.title: Does Apple Intelligence Label AI-Edited Photos?
item.description: Apple says AI-edited Photos and Image Playground creations will include hidden SynthID watermarks.

item.title: Does Instagram Map Show Your Location From Photos?
item.description: Instagram Map can show location-tagged content, but that is different from sharing your live or last-active location.

item.title: Can Your iPhone Prove a Photo Is Real?
item.description: Apple Reference Image can verify some photos taken on iPhone 18 Pro, but it is not an AI detector. What photo proof means for AI images, social posts, and vibe-check apps.

item.title: Can Apps See Hidden Photos on iPhone?
item.description: Hidden photos are locked in the Photos app, and iPhone photo permissions still matter.

item.title: What Is Captured by Me on iPhone?
item.description: Captured by Me is an iOS 27 Photos filter for pictures taken with your iPhone camera. What it means for finding cleaner photos to edit, share, or use in photo apps.

item.title: Can Smart Glasses Record You?
item.description: Smart glasses can record photos or video from the wearer's point of view, so consent, posting choices, and app privacy settings matter.

item.title: Do AI Photo Apps Need AI Act Labels?
item.description: The EU AI Act transparency rules start applying on August 2, 2026. Here is what AI photo app users should know about labels, deepfakes, and honest vibe-check posts.

item.title: What Is AI Slop?
item.description: AI slop is low-effort AI-generated content that makes feeds feel fake, repetitive, or misleading.

item.title: Can AI Use Your Instagram Photos?
item.description: Meta pulled back a July 2026 feature that let people reference public Instagram accounts in AI images, but public social photos still deserve careful privacy settings and context.

item.title: Should You Give an AI Photo App Full Photo Access?
item.description: Most AI photo apps do not need your whole camera roll for a single edit, aura card, or vibe check.

item.title: Can Photo Apps See Your Location?
item.description: Photo apps may receive location metadata when you share or upload an image.

item.title: Do AI Photo Apps Need Labels on TikTok?
item.description: TikTok asks creators to label realistic AI-generated or significantly AI-edited content.

item.title: Can Apps See All Your iPhone Photos?
item.description: An iPhone app sees your whole photo library only with Full Access. How Limited Access, the photo picker, and privacy labels work.
